name: Cycle of spiders as a cat state
summary: A cycle of N three-legged Z-spiders is 2-fault-equivalent to a single N-legged spider (a cat state).
description: A cycle of $N$ phase-free Z-spiders, each with one leg, equals a single $N$-legged spider. Under edge-flip noise this is a **$w$-fault equivalence for $w = 2$** (the paper writes $\widehat{=}$ with subscript 2): a single fault on the cycle is either detected or equivalent to a single fault on the spider, whatever $N$ is. For $N = 4$ and $N = 5$ the cycle is even [fully fault-equivalent](../fe-four-legged-spider/). In the language of the paper, this is the case $t = 1$ of fault-tolerant cat-state preparation: a loop cannot be cut by a single fault, so any number of legs can be attached to it, giving vertex ratio $r_1 = 0$.
parameter_notes: Shown for N = 6; holds for any N.

source.location: Sec. 5.2 (Graphs of Z-spiders as fault-tolerant CAT states)
